calls.prompt:
Company: Brightside Foods Co.

US mid-size packaged food company (~900 employees, plants in Ohio and Georgia). Makes hot dogs and sausages, brightly colored gummy candy, and pecan-and-apple snack bars. Buys pecans, apples and corn from US farms. Sells through grocery chains and convenience stores (many customers pay with SNAP / food stamps). Runs its own fleet of 40 delivery trucks. No restaurants, no alcohol, no exports.

Rules that APPLY:
- FDA food additive and color additive rules (dyes in candy, casings, meat)
- Food labeling and food safety rules for packaged food and meat products
- EPA pesticide residue limits on crops we buy (pecans, apples, corn)
- USDA marketing orders and grading for pecans and apples
- SNAP rules that change what shoppers can buy or who qualifies (affects demand)
- Workplace safety and labor rules for food plants; trucking safety rules for our fleet

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Aviation, airspace, aircraft airworthiness
- Banking, securities, crypto, sanctions
- Medicare/Medicaid payment rules, medical devices
- Mining, offshore oil and gas, fisheries
- Broadcast/TV licensing

Affected areas and owners:
- food-safety: Additives, dyes, labeling, food safety → Maria Chen (Food Safety & Regulatory)
- sourcing: Ingredients from farms, pesticide limits, crop rules → Tom Alvarez (Sourcing)
- sales: Retail channels, SNAP, pricing → Aisha Grant (Sales Compliance)
- operations: Plant safety, labor, trucking fleet → Ben Kowalski (Operations)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if it is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-11-13, or a final rule that took effect within the 30 days before 2026-11-13; otherwise High for final rules, Medium for proposed rules and for notices with a deadline, Low for anything else), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.
calls.output:
I found six Federal Register documents in the 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-13 window that affect Brightside. The search tool isn't a full Federal Register query, so the list may not be complete. I found nothing in the window for OSHA, FSIS, AMS pecan or apple orders, or FDA labeling. All six are Critical because each is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline within 90 days of 2026-11-13.

**1. 2026-22865: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene**
- URL: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22865/color-additive-petition-from-environmental-defense-fund-et-al-request-to-amend-the-color-additive
- Key deadline: The orders are effective January 11, 2027, and comments are due December 12, 2026. I'm using Dec 12, 2026 as the key date.
- Tier: Critical (rule, deadline under 90 days).
- Owner: food-safety (Maria Chen).
- Reason: FDA removed the authorized use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. FDA denied the requests to remove the extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin. The apple connection is indirect, through fruit-marking inks.
- Action: Confirm with color and ink suppliers that no methylene chloride is used before Jan 11, 2027, and decide by Dec 12 whether to file comments.

**2. 2026-22866: Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride**
- URL: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22866/color-additive-petition-from-the-international-association-of-color-manufacturers-request-to-amend
- Key deadline: Dec 12, 2026 for comments, and Jan 11, 2027 effective date, per the same law-firm summary as item 1.
- Tier: Critical (rule, deadline under 90 days).
- Owner: food-safety (Maria Chen).
- Reason: FDA removed the authorized uses of methylene chloride, trichloroethylene, and ethylene dichloride as extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin. Those natural colors may be used in hot dogs, sausages, gummies or snack bars.
- Action: Check that the annatto, paprika and turmeric colorants we buy are made without these solvents, and update supplier specifications.

**3. 2026-22936: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility (proposed rule)**
- URL: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22936
- Key deadline: Written comments are due on or before December 10, 2026.
- Tier: Critical (proposed rule, deadline under 90 days).
- Owner: sales (Aisha Grant).
- Reason: The proposal would limit categorical eligibility to households that receive TANF assistance, as defined at 45 CFR 260.31. That could shrink SNAP participation among shoppers at our grocery and convenience-store customers.
- Action: Model the possible volume loss by channel and decide by Dec 10 whether to comment, alone or through a trade group.

**4. 2026-22944: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults (proposed rule)**
- URL: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22944
- Key deadline: Written comments must be received on or before December 10, 2026.
- Tier: Critical (proposed rule, deadline under 90 days).
- Owner: sales (Aisha Grant).
- Reason: It would codify USDA's implementation of One Big Beautiful Bill Act changes to the three-month SNAP time limit for certain participants. That could further reduce SNAP-funded demand.
- Action: Add it to the SNAP demand-risk model alongside item 3 and decide on comments by Dec 10.
- Caveat: I inferred the document number from the govinfo file name (2026-22944.pdf), where this rule starts on page 72439. Please check it on federalregister.gov.

**5. 2026-23120: Ethephon; Pesticide Tolerances (final rule)**
- URL: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23120/ethephon-pesticide-tolerances
- Key deadline: The rule is effective November 13, 2026, and objections and hearing requests are due January 12, 2027.
- Tier: Critical (the rule took effect within the 30 days before 11/13, and its deadline is under 90 days).
- Owner: sourcing (Tom Alvarez).
- Reason: The new tolerance is for figs, which we don't buy. However, EPA is revising 40 CFR 180.300 so that compliance with ethephon tolerances is determined by measuring only ethephon. Apples are a registered ethephon use. This is a marginal item for the apple supply.
- Action: Tell apple growers and testing labs about the revised tolerance expression. No objection is likely to be needed.

**Also noted, but not Federal Register documents:**
- USDA announced on Nov 13 a 90-day compliance extension for SNAP retailers on the May 2026 stocking-standards rule. Retailers must comply by February 11, 2027. I found only a retailer notice, not a Federal Register document, so it isn't in the list. Aisha Grant may still want to track it, since it affects our SNAP retail customers.
- A Nov 9 FMCSA notice on driver exemption applications for epilepsy and seizure disorders was published in the window. It doesn't impose obligations on a private fleet, so I left it out.
